subject: Reserved capacity SKU morph and price-corridor authorization request
messages:
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@auroraai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@auroraai.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: flexible SKU morph + price corridor for reserved capacity

Hi Vivek,

Following up from our call this morning — AuroraAI is preparing a 12-month reserved capacity commitment and we want to build in some operational flexibility. Two asks from our side:

1) SKU morph option: ability to shift up to 20% of committed GPU SKUs between compatible instance families every quarter (for example: A100->A800-equivalent) without penalty, subject to capacity availability.

2) Price corridor: a capped pass-through mechanism if market GPU spot prices move beyond +/- 18% relative to contract baseline; we propose a shared corridor where Redwood absorbs the first 9% and AuroraAI absorbs the next 9%, with escalation to executive review beyond that.

Attached is our initial capacity plan (v2) and a one-page term sketch. We need to lock commercial language and an internal approval path — Procurement asked me to get this authorized by finance/sales before we put it into the SOW.

Can you confirm who needs to sign off on the corridor and the SKU morph, and whether Redwood can accept a quarterly SKU-morph window?

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Park
Head of Infrastructure
AuroraAI

Attachments: aurora_capacity_plan_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), price-corridor-draft-terms.pdf (pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@auroraai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: flexible SKU morph + price corridor for reserved capacity

Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and the plan. Short answer: we can operationalize a quarterly SKU-morph window and a limited price corridor, but we need an approval ladder for the corridor thresholds and a small guardrail on SKU morph to preserve capacity SLAs.

Internally, I need:
- Sales approval for discount/credit mechanics (Marissa)
- Finance signoff on corridor exposure and accounting treatment of pass-throughs (Kimberly)
- Product/Infra confirmation on compatible SKU families and migration OSS operational costs (Aditya)

Marissa / Kimberly / Aditya — can you review the attached plan and the corridor sketch? My recommendation: accept 15% SKU morph (not 20%) with a rolling quarterly window and cap SKU morph for initial 3 quarters to 10% to limit ramp risk. For the price corridor, agree to Redwood absorb up to a 7% downside, AuroraAI absorb next 11% (split 7/11 instead of 9/9) — this gives Redwood a little more protection at inception.

I'll assemble a short approval memo once you confirm.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Global Capacity & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: aurora_capacity_plan_v2.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Alicia Park <alicia.park@auroraai.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: flexible SKU morph + price corridor for reserved capacity

Vivek / team — quick read:
- I can support a limited SKU-morph window but we need to trade for a small revenue concession. Proposal: a fixed 5% credit applied to the committed monthly invoice for each quarter where SKU-morph is exercised beyond a 5% threshold (credit capped at 10% of that month). This preserves economics and creates a tangible cost for frequent morphing.
- Price corridor split: lean toward Redwood absorbing the first 6% and AuroraAI next 12% — but we can land anywhere between Vivek's 7/11 and my 6/12 after Kimberly's finance check.

Next steps: Kimberly, can you run a quick P&L exposure for the 6/12 and 7/11 corridors for the attached capacity profile? I want a one-slide risk table for executive approval.

—Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: price-corridor-draft-terms.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: flexible SKU morph + price corridor for reserved capacity

Team — ran the exposure models (summary below). I attached an annotated SKU map and a condensed P&L. High level:

- Baseline: AuroraAI's committed monthly run-rate per plan = $1.1M.
- Corridor scenarios over 12 months (simulated price shocks):
  * Minor swing (+/-10%): net impact within working capital — no exec escalation.
  * Moderate swing (10-20%): 7/11 split yields Redwood expected hit of ~$1.6M over 12 months (worst-case simulated), 6/12 yields ~$1.9M.
  * Severe swing (>20%): exposure jumps non-linearly; recommend reserve clause that triggers executive review and temporary throttling/fallback to non-reserved routing if external GPU market is unavailable.

Recommendations: accept a conservative 7/11 split with a 15% SKU-morph operational cap (10% first 3 quarters as Vivek suggested) and include an executive-escalation clause beyond 20% realized market move. If Sales wants a wider morph or softer corridor, we need an up-front non-refundable activation credit equal to one month of committed fees.

I can present the P&L slide at 4pm if you want to huddle.

Kimberly Park
Head of Finance, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: annotated-sku-map.csv, price-impact-summary.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@auroraai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: flexible SKU morph + price corridor for reserved capacity

Alicia — looping back with an agreed internal position to move into legal/SOW language. Agreed items:

- SKU-morph: quarterly window; initial 3-quarters soft cap at 10%, thereafter rolling cap at 15%. Allowed families: A100, A800-equivalent, B720 (product to confirm). Operational lead: Aditya will draft an ops runbook and migration SLOs.
- Price corridor: Redwood to absorb first 7% of market delta, AuroraAI next 11% (7/11 split). Beyond 20% cumulative monthly delta, executive escalation and temporary throttling/fallback allowed.
- Commercial trade: AuroraAI to provide a one-month non-refundable activation credit to start the reserved pool; SKU-morph credits apply per Marissa's proposal (5% credit beyond 5% usage in a quarter, capped at 10% of that month).

If that aligns, I'll ask Legal to start a short amendment and loop Kimberly for the final P&L appendix. Alicia — can your Procurement team confirm the activation credit and we'll send a redline-ready term sheet by EOD Monday?

Thanks all — good collaboration.

Vivek
VP, Global Capacity & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
